ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (211) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, italics, footnote markers, and deletion markup preserved.
Translated fresh from the Russian; where a passage coincides with the calendar or a finished story, the reviewed R003 English was reused and changed only where this text differs.

Tolstoy's terms are held: «разумение» (razumenie, 'understanding'), «совершенствование» (sovershenstvovanie, 'perfecting'), «государственное устройство» (gosudarstvennoe ustroystvo, 'state organization'); the Kant passage of 31 January and the opening thought of 9 March reuse the finished calendar English, changed only where this text differs. Attributions follow the print, with «Томас Бейн» (Tomas Beyn, a slip for Пейн, Peyn) given as Thomas Paine and «Тит Ливий» (Tit Liviy) as Titus Livius; the passage signed «Чаннинг» (Channing) is kept under his name, although its first paragraphs are from Paine's *Age of Reason*. The file title misprints «издеателем» for «издателем» (izdatelem, 'by the publisher').

Source observation: [subtitle] The file subtitle misprints «издеателем» for «издателем» (izdatelem, 'by the publisher'); the heading in [1] has the correct «ИЗДАТЕЛЕМ». Translated as 'by the Publisher'.

Source observation: [78] «людей, желающих преобразования его» (its transformation): singular «его» though the antecedent «правительства» (governments) is plural; translated as printed ('to transform it').

Source observation: [85] «ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЕ» ('Conclusion') stands between the two opening thoughts of 25 March and its numbered thoughts, followed by two page markers (p. 429 with no text); possibly misplaced or a remnant of the source layout. Translated as printed.

Source observation: [97]-[100] Signed «Чаннинг» (Channing), but [97] (from 'For a person's happiness') and [98] are from Thomas Paine, The Age of Reason, Part I ('Infidelity does not consist in believing, or in disbelieving...'); [99] also echoes Paine. Attribution kept as printed.

Source observation: [131] «под видом либерализма науки, философии, религии»: possibly a dropped comma after «либерализма» (liberalizma, 'liberalism'); translated as printed ('the liberalism of science, philosophy, religion').

Source observation: [136] «Томас Бейн» (Tomas Beyn) is a slip for «Пейн» (Peyn, Paine): the quotation is the opening of Paine's Common Sense ('Society is produced by our wants, and government by our wickedness'). Rendered 'Thomas Paine.'
Source observation: [137] «не участие» printed as two words (cf. «неучастием», neuchastiem, in [133]); translated 'nonparticipation'.
